correctness.rationale: For 3d plant incidences distributed among 3d-3 nonisolated pollinators, the excess ∑(deg−1)=3 forces exactly T/D/S/H up to label symmetry. Conditional binomial survivor probabilities and all seven Hall subset inequalities give the displayed exact reliability for T and factored positive T−D,T−S,T−H differences, for every integer d≥3 and 0<q<1; q=0,1 tie. Independent survival-mask enumeration gives T,D,S,H=(39,28,37,37)/64 for d=3, q=1/2 and T=415/512 at d=4, matching the formula; this is finite corroboration, the all-d proof is the classification and factorization.
residual_risks: The factorized Hall sums were checked against d=3,4 independent enumerations but not every polynomial coefficient for arbitrary d; analytic identity must bear that range.

value.rationale: A universal optimizer for post-loss capacity-one service is mathematically motivated by Hall feasibility and redundancy allocation: a local cyclic overlap design beats both concentrated-pair and triple-core architectures for every loss probability, including a strict boundary classification. This is stronger than computing a single network reliability and need not predict field ecology.
residual_risks: Real pollinators can serve more than one plant, so ecological applicability depends on the explicit capacity-one model.
